messages.subject: [acs-r] Can't download data before 2012
messages.body_plain:
Greetings!

I can?t seem to download data before 2012. When I run the following code:

regions <- geo.make(us = 1)
acs.fetch(endyear = 2011, span = 1, geography=regions, table.number= ?B01003?)

I get this error message: "Warning message:
In (function (endyear, span = 5, dataset = "acs", keyword, table.name,  :
  As of the date of this version of the acs package
  no variable?"

It works just fine if I try 2012 or later. I also have the same problem with other tables (e.g., B01001, B17018, B19057). What am I missing?

Also, if this isn?t the right place to ask questions, I apologize.

Thank you for your help!

--
Jacob D. Curtis
Graduate Research Assistant
Research, Evaluation, Measurement & Statistics, Educational Psychology
Texas Tech University

messages.subject: [acs-r] working examples of extracting 1990 and 2000 census data
messages.subject_clean: [acs-r] working examples of extracting 1990 and 2000 census data
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
Two questions that I'm guessing you all know something about:
I am yet to find any working examples around the web for accessing 1990
census tables at the block group level with the acs package. I'm having a
great deal of trouble identifying the correct table names for 1990, if
anyone has been successful at this.

I have lat/long and street address data for a few thousand of addresses.
Are there suggested methods for an amateur at this stuff to convert these
into block groups codes? I've found some online tools but only for 2000 or
2010 block groups.
Thanks!



*Chris Cambron, MSW, MPP*
Doctoral Candidate
Social Development Research Group
School of Social Work   |  University of Washington
ccambron at uw.edu  |  www.sdrg.org

messages.subject: [acs-r] working examples of extracting 1990 and 2000 census data
messages.subject_clean: [acs-r] working examples of extracting 1990 and 2000 census data
messages.body_plain:
If your addresses are all from a single metro, you might try contacting its Metropolitan Planning Organization (MPO) or Council of Governments (COG) to see if they have historical block-group files for their area.  I see you are at the University of Washington.  The MPO/COG in the Seattle areas is the Puget Sound Regional Council (http://www.psrc.org/ ).

Frank

Kansas City, MO 64105

Hi all,
Two questions that I'm guessing you all know something about:
I am yet to find any working examples around the web for accessing 1990 census tables at the block group level with the acs package. I'm having a great deal of trouble identifying the correct table names for 1990, if anyone has been successful at this.

I have lat/long and street address data for a few thousand of addresses. Are there suggested methods for an amateur at this stuff to convert these into block groups codes? I've found some online tools but only for 2000 or 2010 block groups.
Thanks!



Chris Cambron, MSW, MPP
Doctoral Candidate
Social Development Research Group
School of Social Work   |  University of Washington

gets pretty spotty as you get closer back to 2011 and earlier.  From
<http://www.census.gov/data/developers/data-sets/acs-1year.2011.html":

  Note: 2011 data are only available for Congressional Districts

Sorry!

messages.subject: [acs-r] Questions for the Census Bureau?
messages.body_plain:
Next week I'm having my first-ever meeting with someone from the Census
Bureau.

I have a list of questions that I'm planning to ask. But I'd also like to
pass along questions from others in the R community that use their data.

If you have any questions you'd like me to pass along, please just leave
them as a comment on this blog post:

http://www.arilamstein.com/blog/2016/11/14/questions-census-bureau/

Ari
